::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 11th 1859  
**From:** Otterbourne Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1859/9
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd),
I am sorry this came just too late to send to you at home as you wished.  It was too late to write and hurry the [people at Derby](organizations/other_108.qmd)to print it, so I could only wait for the chance of its coming in time.  The last thing I heard about it was from [the writer](people/person_1513.qmd) of the [Cheshire Pilgrims](other_books/otherbook_180.qmd)[^1]  [Frances Dysart](other_books/otherbook_265.qmd) is delightful.[^2]  I am glad you are going to have a little breathing time out of London.  You see I shall have another proof in a month’s time to send you

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Envelope addressed to Miss Ann Carter Smith/ Sutton Coldfield/ Warwickshire and postmarked Winchester 11 July 1859 and Birmingham 12 July 1859. It also contains a head and shoulders photograph of CMY in old age.
[^2]: Frances Maria Wilbraham (d.1905), the author of *The Cheshire Pilgrims, or, Sketches of Crusading Life in the Thirteenth Century*  (1862), which ran in *MP* (July 1859-1860)
[^3]: Frances Dysart is the heroine of *Will No One Do Likewise*?
